issueTitle: webtools-http: published test-fixtures variant with the fake transport, virtual clock, `.http` fixtures, recorder and the publication check
function: A consumer of `webtools-http` cannot yet test its providers without the network: the transport port `HttpTransport` that #62 built has no implementation, and nothing gives a test one clock for the cache, the budget and `delay` (#55 architecture §6.7). This run adds a published test-fixtures variant of `webtools-http`, one coordinate with the capability `webtools-http-test-fixtures`, holding the virtual clock, the scripted fake transport, the `.http` fixture codec and the gated recorder, and a publication check in `build-logic` that guards the experimental publishing API the variant rests on. Unit 4 of #55: one system, the fixtures variant; the loopback factories and the budget fakes join it in later units.

rows.name: The test-fixtures compilation and its publication

gap.summary: `webtools-http` has a main `commonMain` and `jvmMain` and their tests, and no test-fixtures compilation or variant, so a consumer has nothing to put on its test classpath. Kotlin has no first-class test-fixtures feature for a multiplatform module (KT-63142, KT-69482 open); what exists is a JVM-only compilation published through the experimental `kotlin.publishing.adhocSoftwareComponent`.
evidence: webtools-http/build.gradle.kts:28-53 — the `commonMain` and `jvmMain` source sets only; no fixtures compilation (baseline)
webtools-http/src/ — `commonMain`, `commonTest`, `jvmMain`, `jvmTest`; no `jvmTestFixtures` (baseline)
../research/kmp-test-fixtures.md F3, F4 — no first-class feature; the publishing hook is experimental through KGP 2.4.21
gap.source: ../research/README.md § Build, publishing and the Java 11 floor; ../architecture.md §6.7

options.name: A hand-built JVM-only `testFixtures` compilation associated with `main`, published as two variants with the capability `webtools-http-test-fixtures` (recipe B)
options.why: One coordinate and one version, and the fixtures' own dependencies, `kotlinx-coroutines-test` 1.10.2 and `mockwebserver3` 5.5.0, reach only the consumer's test classpath through Maven scope mapping as optional entries. The association lets the fixtures reach `internal` declarations such as `HttpSyntax`. The variants set `TargetJvmVersion` from `JAVA_FLOOR`, which the target's attribute does not reach, and the fixtures jar joins `verifyJavaFloor`.

options.name: Gradle's `java-test-fixtures` plugin beside the multiplatform plugin (recipe A)
options.why: The consumer contract is identical (measured), but it re-implements an internal Gradle variant mapping and carries a workaround for KGP 2.2.0, which publishes its runtime variant without dependencies.
options.wins: If recipe B stops working on a later Kotlin Gradle plugin: A is the fallback.

options.name: A separate `webtools-http-testing` artifact
options.why: What every surveyed multiplatform library does, but requirement 3 asks for one coordinate and one version.
options.wins: If the experimental publishing API were removed without replacement.

options.name: Fixtures in common code, for every target
options.why: `mockwebserver3` 5.5.0 is JVM-only, and no mechanism publishes common-source fixtures as a Gradle fixtures variant; a future non-JVM target gets no fixtures from this mechanism.

options.name: A sources jar for the fixtures, through an extra adhoc variant
options.why: The fixtures jar ships without sources or javadoc, as Gradle's own plugin publishes it and as Central hosts such artifacts; the extra variant is additive if Central's validator refuses the jar at the first release.

options.name: Add `org.jetbrains.kotlin.platform.type` or `org.gradle.jvm.environment` to the fixtures variants
options.why: It moves the variants towards the default Kotlin ones, which the Kotlin Gradle plugin's KDoc asks added variants not to match, and gains nothing: a missing attribute is compatible, and every measured consumer selects the variants by their capability.

options.name: Recipe B extracted into `build-logic` as a convention
options.why: Only this module has fixtures in 1.0.0, so the module's own build file carries the block, as the convention plugin's java-floor comment already expects.
options.wins: When a second module publishes fixtures: a follow-up the plan leaves.

impact.summary: The root module of `webtools-http`, new and unreleased, gains a test-fixtures variant: two variants with the capability `webtools-http-test-fixtures` and a `-test-fixtures.jar`, whose test libraries reach a consumer's test classpath only. The main variants, the ABI dump and the three existing artifacts do not change, and no version moves. Inside the repository, `build`, `check` and `:webtools-http:check` also run the fixtures-publication check.

release.note: `webtools-http` 1.0.0 stays new and unreleased until #55's stack is complete; it is not a release candidate at this landing

downstream.summary: The root module's metadata gains `testFixturesApiElements` and `testFixturesRuntimeElements`, each with the capability, `org.gradle.jvm.version` 11 and the one `-test-fixtures.jar`; every published file is signed. The `-jvm` module, the main variants and the ABI dump do not change.

downstream.who: Gradle consumers of `webtools-http` 1.0.0, once it is released
downstream.summary: `testFixtures(...)` selects the fixtures; `kotlinx-coroutines-test` 1.10.2 and `mockwebserver3` 5.5.0 reach the test classpath only, and the root POM lists them as optional. A Maven build cannot select a variant by capability, so it cannot use the fixtures.
Nothing changes: no source, build-script or test change in the three modules, and no version moves.

`./gradlew build`, `check` and `:webtools-http:check` run `:build-logic:fixturesPublicationCheck`: about a minute when one of its inputs changed, `UP-TO-DATE` otherwise, and a first run on a host downloads into the TestKit home and BouncyCastle once. The root project gains no plugin and no task.

downstream.who: A build that includes WebTools, such as BotTools' development composite
downstream.summary: The check never runs there and no configuration-time message appears: the edge is declared only when WebTools is the root build.

They build on the fixtures: unit 6 adds the loopback factories and the `MockWebServer` helpers, units 7 and 8 pass `VirtualClock` to the cache and the budget and re-run the three-clocks proof, unit 8 adds the budget fakes, unit 9 scripts the fake and unit 10 consumes the variant.

adaptation.summary: Each implementer of a gated port carries its own `@OptIn`, every public declaration states its visibility and carries KDoc, and the fixtures' dependencies stay the three the check asserts.

adaptation.who: A consumer that records or commits `.http` fixtures
adaptation.summary: It adds `**/fixtures/**/*.http -text` to its `.gitattributes`, and a build that records declares `WEBTOOLS_HTTP_RECORD` as an input of its test tasks, or Gradle skips them as up to date when only the variable changed.

No hand-written fake of `HttpTransport` or `WallClock` exists to move onto the fixtures; `webtools-udp`'s clock, the `testing/support/` helpers and `SampleProject.withLocalPublishing()` stay as they are.
